Sun, Moon and Venus all exalted. A chart that isn't fighting itself.

30 APR 1987 · NAGPUR, MAHARASHTRA

TL;DR

Four planets at full strength. Almost nobody gets that.

Most kundlis on this site are built on friction — a debilitated Sun, a weak Venus, one planet dragging against another. Rohit Sharma's janam kundli barely has any of that.
His Sun is exalted in Aries. His Moon is exalted in Taurus. His Venus is exalted in Pisces. And his Jupiter sits in Pisces too — its own sign. Four strong placements out of nine planets, in a chart most astrologers would call unusually clean.

Read as a lens, not a verdict, it tracks something he's said about his own game for years: he's the "unhurried" one — the batter who looks like he has more time than the bowler.

2011 · THE SNUB

Left out of the World Cup, in his own city

Not selected for the 2011 squad
  • India won the 2011 World Cup at Wankhede Stadium — Rohit Sharma's home ground — and he wasn't in the squad.
  • He's called it the saddest moment of his career: the final happening in his own backyard, without him.
🔭 Deep in his Rahu stretch. Rahu is the chaos planet — it can hand you fame and take away a seat at the table in the same breath.

2013–14 · THE RECORD

Moved to open. Broke the sport.

264 highest individual score in ODI history
  • Promoted to open the batting in 2013 after six years as an inconsistent middle-order finisher — and immediately started scoring differently.
  • 13 November 2014, Eden Gardens: 264 off 173 balls against Sri Lanka, still the biggest individual score ODI cricket has ever seen. He now owns three of the format's handful of double centuries.
🔭 Still Rahu, but the sub-period had turned. The same "chaos" planet that benched him in 2011 was now handing him the record books.

2021–24 · THE CROWN

Full captaincy, then a World Cup with his name on it

T20 champion as captain, June 2024
  • Took over India's T20I captaincy in November 2021, then ODI and Test captaincy in February 2022 — all three formats, right as a new mahadasha began.
  • Led India to the T20 World Cup title in Barbados on 29 June 2024, then retired from T20Is on the spot, on top.
🔭 The opening years of Jupiter — his own best-placed planet, own sign, expansive by classical reading. The captaincy era runs entirely inside it.

2025–26 · THE RESET

Dropped, retired, back at Lord's

138 at Lord's, mid-2026, mid-retirement chatter
  • Left himself out of the deciding Sydney Test in January 2025 after a poor run, retired from Tests that May, then handed the ODI captaincy to Shubman Gill in October 2025.
  • Still won the 2025 Champions Trophy as ODI captain along the way, received the Padma Shri in 2026, and — after a rough Edgbaston knock drew "retire gracefully" calls — answered with 138 off 110 at Lord's weeks later, still chasing 2027.
🔭 Still Jupiter, now in a Mercury sub-period (Dec 2025–Mar 2028). Mercury inside your best mahadasha reads as quick swings, fast recoveries — not a collapse.
The tea ☕

The closest thing he's had to drama

No affairs, no crime, no boycott campaigns — his "messy bits" are mostly just a very public argument about when a great career should end. What the chart says about the pattern, not the gossip.

🏏 Rested, dropped, or retiring? The Sydney call
What's public

In January 2025, with the bat gone quiet through the Border-Gavaskar series, Rohit became the first Indian captain to voluntarily leave himself out of a Test XI — the series decider in Sydney.

He said on air it "was not a retirement decision." Four months later, in May 2025, he retired from Test cricket anyway, ahead of the tour of England.

What the chart hints

He was moving into a fresh sub-period inside his strong Jupiter mahadasha. Jupiter periods are read as ones where you get to choose the ending rather than have it chosen for you.

A chart with this much dignity doesn't usually get dragged out — it walks out on its own clock. That tracks with how this one played out.

👑 The armband goes to Gill
What's public

In October 2025, the BCCI named Shubman Gill India's ODI captain — a generational handover aimed squarely at the 2027 World Cup. Rohit stayed in the playing XI, no drama, no farewell tour.

What the chart hints

Jupiter is the planet of expansion and generosity, not territory. Handing over a title while staying useful is a very Jupiter way to manage a succession — making room rather than being pushed out of it.

📉 "Retire gracefully" — then 138 at Lord's
What's public

A laboured 11 off 21 balls in the first ODI of the 2026 England tour drew fierce fan backlash and calls to hand his opening slot to Yashasvi Jaiswal for good. Reports said selectors had signalled his future beyond the tour wasn't part of their planning.

He pushed back publicly on the retirement talk. Weeks later, at the third ODI at Lord's, he made 138 off 110 balls and said his sights are still on the 2027 World Cup.

What the chart hints

This whole stretch sits inside his current Jupiter–Mercury sub-period (Dec 2025–Mar 2028) — computed, not guessed. Mercury moves fast; a bad month and a brilliant one back to back is exactly its signature.

A note on all three. None of this is a scandal — it's a debate about timing, which is the one thing a dasha ladder is actually built to describe. We're reading eras, not predicting his next innings.
Certified comeback arcs

Left out once. Won it twice anyway.

🚫 → 🏆  The 2011 snub, answered in 2024 and 2025

  • Watched the 2011 World Cup final from outside the squad, at his own home ground.
  • Thirteen years later he lifted the 2024 T20 World Cup as captain — then the 2025 Champions Trophy as ODI captain too.
  • The only Indian captain to close out an ICC white-ball trophy drought that had run since 2013 with two titles inside eighteen months.

🔭 The chart bit: the whole arc runs from the tail of Rahu (the snub) into the strength of Jupiter (both trophies). Chaos handing off to expansion.

🐌 → ⚡  The finisher nobody could place, becomes the best opener alive

  • Six years in the middle order, dropped and recalled repeatedly, tagged inconsistent by pretty much every pundit in the country.
  • Moved to open the innings in 2013. Inside eighteen months he had two ODI double centuries; inside a decade, three — a record nobody else in the format's history has more than one of.
  • Also the only batter with five centuries in a single World Cup (2019).

🔭 The chart bit: his exalted Moon in Taurus, sharing the sign with Mars — instinct and force in the same room. Reads as timing that looks unhurried right up until the ball is gone.

Three planets sit together in Pisces alone — Jupiter, Venus and Rahu. Stack that against a Sun-Mercury pair in Aries and a Moon-Mars pair in Taurus, and nine planets end up occupying just five signs. A clustered, top-heavy chart, and an unusually strong one.

Actually learn this

Astrology, but make it make sense

Zero background needed. Read this once and you can decode the birth chart above yourself — no astrologer required.

LESSON 01

What a birth chart even is

A kundli — birth chart, janam kundli, whatever your family calls it — is a photo of the sky from the exact place and moment someone was born. Where every planet was sitting, frozen.

Vedic astrology reads that photo as the raw material a person was handed, not a script for their life.

His: 30 April 1987, Nagpur. That sky had the Sun in Aries, the Moon in Taurus, Venus in Pisces — all three at full strength. That's most of the story right there.
LESSON 02

The planets, and what each one does

Nine of them. Think of them as nine departments, each running one part of a life.

LESSON 03

Why "which sign" actually matters

Every planet has signs where it's comfortable and signs where it struggles. Same planet, wildly different output.

  • Exalted — its single best possible sign. As strong as that planet ever gets.
  • Own sign — home ground. Comfortable, reliable, does its job without a fight.
  • Everywhere else — a guest. Functional, not special, which is where most planets in most charts sit.
His scorecard: three exalted planets (Sun, Moon, Venus) and one in its own sign (Jupiter). Most charts on this site — and most charts, period — get zero or one of those. He got four, which is closer to the theoretical ceiling than to average.
LESSON 04

Dashas — why timing is the whole game

Your planets don't all act at once. They take turns running your life, for years at a stretch, in a fixed order and for fixed lengths set by where the Moon sat at birth. Vedic astrology calls a planet's turn a dasha.

His turns, computed:
Moon 1987–96 · Mars 1996–2003 · Rahu 2003–21 · Jupiter 2021–2037 (current) · Saturn from 2037

Everything from the 2011 World Cup snub to the 264 record happened under Rahu — the chaos planet. Everything since the full captaincy handover in 2022 has run under Jupiter — his single strongest placement.
LESSON 05

Sub-periods — the chapters inside the chapter

A sixteen-year mahadasha is too blunt to be useful on its own, so it splits into shorter stretches, each handed to a different planet. That's where the year-to-year story actually lives.

Right now: he's in a Jupiter–Mercury sub-period, running 16 December 2025 to 23 March 2028. Mercury is quick, adaptable, a little restless — inside an otherwise steady Jupiter era, that reads as sharp short-term swings rather than a change in direction. The 2026 form questions and the Lord's comeback both sit inside this exact window.
LESSON 06

What we genuinely can't tell you

Here's where most celebrity astrology sites quietly cheat, and we won't.

A chart has two halves. Which sign each planet is in — that only needs the date, so everything above is solid, and we double-checked it holds across his entire birth day. And the houses, which need the exact minute of birth.

No birth time has ever been published for Rohit Sharma. So on this page you will not see us say "his career house" or "his 7th house of marriage" — that would be a guess dressed up as a fact. Other sites publish exact birth times for him anyway; ask them where they got it.
LESSON 07

So — is Rohit Sharma manglik?

One of the most-searched questions about him, and the honest answer is that nobody can give it to you straight.

"Manglik" depends on which house Mars sits in — and houses need the birth time. Without it, this genuinely cannot be answered, for him or for compatibility checks with anyone else's kundli.

What we can say: his Mars sits in Taurus, alongside an exalted Moon. Whether that lands in a manglik house depends entirely on an hour nobody has published. Any site giving you a confident yes or no picked a birth time from somewhere and didn't tell you.

Quick answers

What people ask about his kundli

FAQ 01

What is Rohit Sharma's birth time and birth chart?

No verified birth time has ever been published for him, so this page sticks to what a date alone settles — his zodiac signs, nakshatra and dasha eras — and skips houses and lagna entirely. His full birth chart, signs-only, is above.

FAQ 02

What is his zodiac sign and nakshatra?

His Moon — the sign Vedic astrology uses as the "rashi" — sits in Taurus, exalted, in the Rohini nakshatra. His Sun sits in Aries, also exalted. Every placement here is computed from his birth date, not copied from another site.

FAQ 03

Is Rohit Sharma manglik?

Unanswerable honestly without a birth time. His Mars sits in Taurus, but whether that falls in a manglik house needs the exact hour of birth, which has never been published. See Lesson 07 above.

FAQ 04

What does his current dasha say about 2026 and 2027?

He's in a Jupiter–Mercury sub-period from December 2025 to March 2028 — Jupiter is his strongest, most expansive placement, with quick-moving Mercury layered inside it. Astrologers would read that as a stretch built for a late push rather than a fade, which lines up with his own stated target of playing the 2027 World Cup. That's a reading, not a prediction.
